llm.summary: This SEO writing skill is broadly coherent, but it includes an explicit AI-detector bypass tool and some under-disclosed external API and credential-handling risks.

dimensions.detail: Local file reads and writes are expected for content processing, and Gemini API use is expected for image generation, but prompts and optional input images are sent to Google without a clear privacy warning; the image script also accepts API keys via command-line arguments and uses open-ended dependency versions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hooks, persistence setup, service registration, or auto-execution behavior were found; installation appears to be a normal skill package with Python scripts and documentation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Most commands are user-directed, but the documented scope is broad and partially inconsistent: SKILL.md references missing video, transcript, and compare scripts, requests curl, and does not clearly define tool boundaries for research, competitor analysis, file I/O, network use, or external services.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No cross-session persistence, background workers, privilege escalation, scheduled tasks, credential harvesting, or broad local indexing behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core SEO/content, title, A/B test, local detection, and image-generation features fit the stated purpose, but the skill repeatedly advertises transforming AI-generated text to bypass AI detectors and the script removes AI/provenance-like artifacts, which is a material misuse and deception-enablement concern.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill carefully before installing. Use it only for transparent, policy-compliant editing, not to misrepresent AI-generated content as human-authored or evade platform, academic, or publisher checks. Prefer GEMINI_API_KEY from a protected environment over --api-key, avoid sending confidential prompts or images to Gemini, and be aware that local output files may be overwritten when you choose an output path.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Accepted in substance: the artifact explicitly markets AI humanization to bypass AI detectors, which is not necessary for legitimate SEO assistance even though it is openly disclosed.
[SQP-3] unexpected: Accepted for the detector-bypass concern; the language-locale observations are lower impact because Chinese title tooling is visible in the docs and related to SEO, though documentation is inconsistent.
[SSD-2] unexpected: Accepted in substance: scripts/humanize.py is explicitly framed as bypassing detection and removes citations, ChatGPT/OpenAI markers, chatbot artifacts, and formatting.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted: removal of citation and platform markers can conceal AI provenance or attribution, which is a material concern in a publishing-focused skill.
[SQP-2] expected: Partially accepted: file reads and writes are normal for user-specified content tools, but external Gemini image generation should more clearly disclose third-party data transfer and overwrite behavior.
[PE3] expected: Downgraded: the code reads only a provided API key or GEMINI_API_KEY for the Gemini client, not broad credential files; this is expected for the image API but should avoid command-line secrets.
[LP3] expected: Partially accepted: the skill's broad capabilities would benefit from explicit permission and data-flow documentation, but no hidden privileged behavior was found.
[T08] expected: Accepted as a supply-chain note: generate_image.py uses open-ended google-genai and pillow dependency constraints, which is not malicious but weakens reproducibility.
[T09] expected: Accepted as a credential-handling note: --api-key is documented and implemented, which can expose the Gemini key through shell history or process logs.
